response.sql: WITH driver_totals AS (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS total_points, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(NULLIF(laps, '\N'), '') AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM results WHERE grid > 12 GROUP BY driverId) SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total_points, AVG(avg_laps) AS avg_of_avg_laps FROM driver_totals;

assumptions.assumption: 'Higher than 12' means grid >= 13, so pit-lane starts (grid = 0) and NULL grids are excluded by the predicate grid > 12.

Missing laps values may be stored as NULL, the string '\N' (the Ergast convention), or an empty string. All three are treated as missing and excluded from the per-driver AVG, because the schema and documentation do not state how missing values are encoded.

Points and laps are aggregated only over the filtered races (grid > 12), not over full-season totals, so driverStandings is not used. A driver whose laps are all missing still counts in the points average but is skipped in the average of average laps.

alternatives.interpretation: Only include drivers who have at least one valid laps value, so the points average uses the same driver set as the average of average laps.
alternatives.sql: WITH driver_totals AS (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS total_points, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(NULLIF(laps, '\N'), '') AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM results WHERE grid > 12 GROUP BY driverId HAVING avg_laps IS NOT NULL) SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total_points, AVG(avg_laps) AS avg_of_avg_laps FROM driver_totals;
